2027 Acura Integra Type S Debuts Minor Changes, Welcomes Limited-Run Heritage Edition
12 photos
Photo: Acura / edited
Acura's most exciting model for 2027 builds on the outgoing Integra Type S in many ways. Redesigned cabin materials and new exterior finishes open the list of changes, followed by several convenience features. The Honda-controlled marque hasn't touched the 2.0-liter turbo inline-four engine or the six-speed transaxle, but Acura did make a case for a special edition that you can only have in yellow.
The 2027 model year ITS is rocking standard yellow brake calipers, accompanied by gloss-black wheels and mirror caps. Hopping inside reveals dark gray trim across the door panels, instrument panel, and shifter surround. There's also a new diamond pattern for the instrument panel, whereas gloss-black knobs for the HVAC system provide additional contrast.
Prospective customers get precisely three redesigned upholstery choices, beginning with Ebony and yellow goodies. Yellow perforations on the seats are joined by yellow stitching for the steering wheel's rim, door panels, shifter boot, and center console. Orchid upholstery includes microsuede stripes in blue, whereas the Red interior theme combines red with contrasting black microsuede.
In regard to convenience, the driver's seat now comes with memory. A memory brake hold function will also make the driver's life easier, and the same can be said about the reverse-tilt functionality for both side mirrors. Under the skin, you get a familiar FWD machine with VTEC oomph.
This year, Acura quotes 320 horsepower at 6,500 revolutions per minute and no fewer than 310 pound-feet (420 Newton-meters) from 2,600 through 4,000 revolutions per minute. Its three-pedal box is a familiar auto rev-matching unit with a limited-slip differential for good measure, so yeah, Acura didn't bother changing what was perfectly so from the outset.
Photo: Acura When it comes to pricing, $54,600 from the outset is a lot for a compact. Adding the $1,395 destination charge results in five bucks under $56,000, and that is before taxes, registration, and similar expenses. The EPA fuel consumption estimates remain unchanged: 21 mpg in the city, 28 highway, and 24 in the combined test cycle, equivalent to 9.8 l/100 km.
Assembled in Ohio alongside the lesser Integra, the Type S is powered by a four-pot mill assembled in Ohio as well. Due to hit dealers in December 2026, the ITS has a surprise in store for us. Celebrating the DC2 Integra Type R, the Heritage Edition is offered in merely 700 units for the US market.
Marking three decades since the DC2 ITR made its American debut, the special edition brings back the spirit of Phoenix Yellow. The company is calling this hue Blazing Phoenix Yellow, and the color represents a more vibrant interpretation of the yellow offered back in the day. This paint option also marks the first time since MY01 that Acura has offered yellow on the Integra.
Black exterior badging, copper-finished alloy wheels boasting a 10-spoke design, and an exclusive titanium shift knob inspired by the JDM ITR are featured. Every Heritage Edition sports the Ebony and yellow interior. $56,900 is the advertised starting price of the most exciting Integra available for 2027, and this version carries the same EPA fuel economy ratings.
Acura intends to showcase the Integra Type S Heritage Edition at Super Street After Dark in Santa Ana, California, on November 19, followed by the LA Auto Show from November 19 through 29. As with the regular ITS, the HE will also reach dealers in December 2026.
